proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true admission lag is shorter/longer or time-varying, a fixed 2-week delay can misalign peak timing and distort rise/decline slopes.
proposals.rationale: Hospitalization-rate target can plausibly lag the infectious proxy by ~2 weeks; SEIRS supports moderate peakiness with potential within-season susceptibility replenishment while staying parsimonious for a 31-week training window.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-delaying can shift peaks too late and force compensatory parameter behavior, degrading early-season fit and short-horizon forecasts.
proposals.rationale: A 3-week delay accommodates longer progression-to-admission timing and reporting latency; SEIRS remains a compact template for single-season dynamics with moderate peaks.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable in a short series, leading to unstable separation of I vs H and overfitting of hospitalization duration/transition rates.
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the hospitalization-rate target to an explicit H compartment, aligning surveillance semantics without requiring an external delay; suitable when admissions dynamics differ from infectious prevalence.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the target corresponds primarily to admissions (not a mixture), I+H can blur interpretation and bias amplitude/peak width, especially during rapid growth/decline.
proposals.rationale: If reported hospitalization rates reflect a mixture of current infectious burden and hospitalized census/admissions effects, observing I+H can provide robustness against mis-specified hospitalization dwell time while still leveraging an H compartment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If immunity waning/reinfection within the season is material, SEIR may under-capture late-season persistence or secondary bumps, causing under-forecasting in the tail.
proposals.rationale: More parsimonious than SEIRS while retaining an incubation stage; delayed_I links latent infectious dynamics to hospitalization-rate timing with minimal compartments for a 31-week training span.
